entry.publicName: Expunge a record you sealed ten years ago

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 943.0585 expressly excepts a later expunction of the same record after at least ten years of qualifying court-ordered sealing from the prior-relief bar. FDLE's FAQ confirms that a record initially ineligible for expunction because adjudication was withheld may become eligible after ten years sealed.

eligibleDispositions: a record that has been under a qualifying court-ordered seal for at least ten years and is otherwise eligible
exclusions: The prior sealing still prevents using the ordinary statutes on a different arrest record.

waitingPeriods.condition: Qualifying court-ordered sealing of the same record

geography.venue: Statewide Florida two-stage process; FDLE first, then circuit or county court in the circuit where the arrest occurred.

destination.name: Florida Department of Law Enforcement, then the circuit or county court in the circuit of arrest
destination.detail: A fresh screening and a new FDLE certificate application, then the later court packet. It is not automatic and relief remains discretionary.

components.notes: A new FDLE certificate application at the ten-year point.
Briefcase eligibility-date reminder at the ten-year point.

participantInputs.question: On what date was the record sealed by court order?
Has the seal remained in force since then?
What was the offence and its statute section?
Have you picked up any new arrests or charges since the record was sealed?
In which county and judicial circuit did the original arrest happen?

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The amendment expressly resolves the former blocker: "FL-3 is a valid same-record bridge... FL-3 is removed from the blocker list." The original review's unresolved once-per-lifetime question is answered by the statute and the FDLE FAQ. The amended output is staged official_pdf_fill with a Briefcase eligibility-date reminder.
